rows.label: Concept
rows.text: An achromatic doublet balances wavelength dispersion with signed lens powers: ω1/f1+ω2/f2=0. It reduces but does not eliminate every colour error.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Contact thin doublet: ω1/f1+ω2/f2=0.
Net power: 1/F=1/f1+1/f2.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Dispersion Definition:** Dispersion is the separation of white light into its constituent colors (spectrum) due to the dependence of the refractive index $n$ on the wavelength $\lambda$ of light ($n(\lambda)$).  ·  **Cauchy's Equation:** For many transparent materials, the refractive index follows Cauchy's equation $n(\lambda) = A + B/\lambda^2 + C/\lambda^4$. This explains why blue light ($\lambda$ smaller) is refracted more than red light ($\lambda$ larger).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Do not omit the negative focal length of the diverging lens.  ·  The simple condition assumes thin lenses in contact.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: f1=+20 cm, ω1=0.02 and ω2=0.04 require f2=−40 cm.  ·  A pair with powers +5 D and −2 D has net +3 D and F≈+0.333 m.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Separated lenses: ω1 f1 + ω2 f2 = 0 is not the contact rule  ·  Contact rule: ω1/f1 + ω2/f2 = 0  ·  Convert units before substituting.  ·  Quote the unit with the result.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: The contact condition uses powers, so the dispersive powers are divided by the focal lengths. If the two lenses are separated by a distance, the condition changes and a Huygens eyepiece uses that separated arrangement. Quoting the contact rule for a separated pair gives the wrong flint lens.  ·  The working relations are Separated lenses: ω1 f1 + ω2 f2 = 0 is not the contact rule and Contact rule: ω1/f1 + ω2/f2 = 0. Name each symbol, convert the data into SI units, and only then substitute.

rows.text: The second lens in this pair is → B  ·  A separated pair → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: An optical pair is achromatic for two chosen colours when their wavelength-dependent deviations cancel and both colours share a final focus. The lenses remain dispersive individually; their effects compensate.  ·  For two thin lenses in contact with signed focal lengths f1,f2 and dispersive powers ω1,ω2, primary achromatism requires ω1/f1+ω2/f2=0. A crown converging lens is commonly paired with a more dispersive flint diverging lens.  ·  Worked design: f1=+20 cm, ω1=0.02 and ω2=0.04 require 0.02/20+0.04/f2=0, giving f2=−40 cm. The negative sign identifies a diverging flint element.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Worked case  ·  **Prism Validity:** The formula for dispersive power $\omega = (n_v - n_r)/(n_y - 1)$ assumes small angle of deviation and that the prism is in air. For non-thin prisms or different mediums, angular dispersion depends on the geometry.  ·  A vector answer needs a direction as well as a magnitude.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A special case, such as a right angle or a steady temperature, has to be stated before it is used.  ·  Two lenses in contact have ω1 = 0.030, f1 = +15 cm and ω2 = 0.045. Find the flint focal length that cancels the colour.  ·  The net power is 1/F=1/f1+1/f2, so the doublet can remain converging while cancelling colour spread. Camera, telescope and microscope objectives use achromatic groups to reduce coloured fringes.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Primary achromatism corrects two selected wavelengths; other colours may still form a secondary spectrum.
